label: Secretory_Carcinoma
answer_markdown:
## Key Facts
- Secretory carcinoma is a salivary gland-type carcinoma defined by ETV6-NTRK3 fusion.
- Commonly presents with microcystic, tubular, and solid structures featuring eosinophilic secretions.
- Positive staining for S100, SOX10, and mammaglobin.
- Typically occurs in middle-aged individuals, with a slight female predilection.
- Differential diagnosis includes mucoepidermoid carcinoma, acinic cell carcinoma, and mucinous adenocarcinoma.

## Terminology
- Secretory carcinoma (SC), also known as mammary analogue secretory carcinoma.
- Previously referred to as "mammary analogue secretory carcinoma," now standardized to "secretory carcinoma."

## Essential and Desirable Diagnostic Criteria
- **Essential:**
  - Eosinophilic vacuolar cells.
  - Bubbly secretions, and microcystic, tubular, solid, and papillary patterns.
  - Positive for S100, SOX10, and mammaglobin [WHO](https://storage.googleapis.com/pathology-hub-0/WHO/WHO_HTML/ENDO/Secretory_Carcinoma.html).
- **Desirable:**
  - Presence of ETV6 translocation [WHO](https://storage.googleapis.com/pathology-hub-0/WHO/WHO_HTML/ENDO/Secretory_Carcinoma.html).

## Etiology/Pathogenesis
- Characterized by ETV6-NTRK3 fusion [Pathoutlines](https://www.pathologyoutlines.com/topic/salivaryglandsmalignant.html).

## Clinical Issues
- **Epidemiology:**
  - Presents at a mean age of 61.5 years (range 36–74).
  - Slight female predominance [WHO](https://storage.googleapis.com/pathology-hub-0/WHO/WHO_HTML/ENDO/Secretory_Carcinoma.html).
- **Presentation:**
  - Often presents as a uninodular mass with possible compression or invasion of adjacent structures [WHO](https://storage.googleapis.com/pathology-hub-0/WHO/WHO_HTML/ENDO/Secretory_Carcinoma.html).

## Macroscopic
- Not specifically detailed in the evidence provided.

## Microscopic
- Composed of microcystic, tubular, and solid structures with eosinophilic secretions.
- Displays bubbly secretions within the tumor architecture [WHO](https://storage.googleapis.com/pathology-hub-0/WHO/WHO_HTML/ENDO/Secretory_Carcinoma.html).

## Ancillary Tests
- **Immunohistochemistry:**
  - Positive for S100, SOX10, and mammaglobin [WHO](https://storage.googleapis.com/pathology-hub-0/WHO/WHO_HTML/ENDO/Secretory_Carcinoma.html).
- **Molecular/Genetics:**
  - ETV6 translocation is a key molecular marker [WHO](https://storage.googleapis.com/pathology-hub-0/WHO/WHO_HTML/ENDO/Secretory_Carcinoma.html).

## Differential Diagnosis
- **Mucoepidermoid Carcinoma:**
  - Distinguished by presence of epidermoid and mucus cells.
  - Typically positive for p63 and p40 [Pathoutlines](https://www.pathologyoutlines.com/topic/salivaryglandsmalignant.html).
- **Acinic Cell Carcinoma:**
  - Features plump cells with vacuolated cytoplasm.
  - May show abundant granular secretory material [Pathoutlines](https://www.pathologyoutlines.com/topic/salivaryglandsmalignant.html).
- **Mucinous Adenocarcinoma:**
  - Other mucin-producing carcinomas must be excluded.
  - Includes presence of mucin-rich combinations [WHO](https://storage.googleapis.com/pathology-hub-0/WHO/WHO_HTML/HN/Mucinous_Adenocarcinoma.html).

cards.title: Mucinous adenocarcinoma
cards.excerpt: Entity: Mucinous adenocarcinoma Section: differential_diagnosis To diagnose MA, other mucin-producing salivary gland carcinomas must be excluded, including mucin-rich mucoepidermoid carcinoma (epidermoid/intermediate cells; p63/p40+), mucinous and rhabdoid variants of salivary duct carcinoma (apocrine cytology; AR+), and the mucinous/secretory pattern of myoepithelial carcinoma (nested/corded pattern; S100, calponin, or SMA+). Metastasis from gastrointestinal, pancreaticobiliary, or lung adenocarcinomas should be ruled out clinically.

cards.title: Malignant — Polygonal cells with enlarged, pleomorphic nuclei and prominent nucleoli
cards.excerpt:
Frequent mitoses and necrosis
Ancillary testing: positive for androgen receptor and GATA3 immunocytochemistry (Cancer Cytopathol 2018;126:627)
Evaluation of AR and HER2 status is recommended for potential targeted therapy (Cancer Cytopathol 2020;128:693)

Squamous cell carcinomas represent 16 - 54% of malignant salivary gland tumors, about 11% of malignant tumors of major salivary glands

cards.title: Squamous cell carcinoma — Usually men (when considering major salivary gland tumors); also associated with AIDS
cards.excerpt:
May occur in Stensen duct
Rapid painless growth with infiltration of surrounding structures, regardless of origin; may cause acute facial paralysis
Aggressive behavior, with 50% 5 year survival (Arch Pathol Lab Med 2001;125:740)

cards.title: Neuroendocrine carcinoma — Essential features
cards.excerpt:
Rare tumor type found predominantly in parotid gland
2 morphologies: small cell neuroendocrine carcinoma and large cell neuroendocrine carcinoma
Positive for neuroendocrine IHC markers; also frequently CK20 positive (Am J Surg Pathol 1997;21:226)
Can be difficult to distinguish from metastatic Merkel cell carcinoma (Am J Surg Pathol 2019;43:682)

cards.title: Salivary duct carcinoma — Epidemiology
cards.excerpt:
Patients are usually in their sixth to seventh decade of life
Mean age: 67.4 years
Range: 33 - 92 years (Am J Surg Pathol 2015;39:705)
M:F = 2.4:1 (AMA Otolaryngol Head Neck Surg 2016;142:489, Am J Surg Pathol 2015;39:705)
Represents ~10% of all salivary glands malignancies

cards.title: Salivary duct carcinoma — Diagnosis
cards.excerpt:
Neck mass that typically leads to imaging studies and fine needle aspiration
Patients may have a long standing history of pleomorphic adenoma that suddenly started to grow rapidly

cards.title: Salivary duct carcinoma — Poor prognostic factors
cards.excerpt:
Higher tumor stage (especially nodal category N2 or higher), 5 year survival rates for stage I is 42% and 23% for stage IV (Cancer 2005;103:2526)
Perineural invasion (especially if the facial nerve is involved and is sacrificed during surgery)

cards.title: Salivary duct carcinoma — Treatment
cards.excerpt:
Total parotidectomy with neck dissection
Adjuvant radiotherapy should be considered, as salivary duct carcinoma is high grade by definition (NCCN: NCCN Guidelines - Head and Neck Cancers [Accessed 7 June 2021])
Chemotherapy (antiandrogens, trastuzumab, anti-BRAF and anti-PIK3CA) for advanced disease as indicated

cards.title: Sclerosing polycystic adenoma — Pathophysiology
cards.excerpt:
Originally believed to be a reactive, nonneoplastic process resembling fibrocystic changes of the breast but evidence suggests it is likely neoplastic (Head Neck Pathol 2020;14:630)
Recurrence rate of up to 30% (Am J Surg Pathol 2006;30:939)
Demonstration of clonality in 6 cases using the human androgen receptor assay (HUMARA) (Am J Surg Pathol 2006;30:939)
Targeted next generation sequencing demonstrated mutations in genes that are well established to be drivers in human neoplasms (Head Neck Pathol 2020;14:630)
